## Which file do I need?

Cognitive Terrain runs in your web browser. Nothing to install.

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.22.1.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.22.1.pdf** |
| Controls and rules on one sheet, two-sided, to keep by the keyboard | **Cognitive-Terrain-Quick-Reference-0.22.1.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.22.1.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |

Two-player games work as long as both players use a 0.22 build (0.22.0, 0.22.1 and so on).

## What's new

- **A new look, same game.** New type throughout (Archivo, with Martian Mono
  for numbers) and a single gold accent for what needs you now: END TURN,
  the next crisis and anything you can press. The panels are flat graphite;
  the red and blue glow stays on the cards, the minimap and each side's
  numbers. The three manuals use the same type and colours.
- **Less to read on screen.** Standing hints and repeated costs are gone from
  the panels. Hover a card for what it does, the areas it works best on, how
  to play it and a real-world example. While you aim a card, the hover card
  on the node gives the result next to the verdict and the side panel keeps
  only why the node matters.
- **A clearer board.** Area names sit on the outer edge of each area, the
  area a crisis tests is outlined in gold with a CRISIS TEST tag beside its
  name, labels have a dark halo, and status icons sit on their own plates so
  they no longer run into names.
- **Result screens rebuilt.** Your move's story card leads with the shift as
  one big number and the spread grade as a row of boxes. What happened shows
  views, likes, comments, shares and posts as tiles, with the arithmetic
  folded away. Week in review sets your moves against theirs, shows your five
  areas as gauges with last week marked, and gives the next crisis with how
  it would go today and what to play. A crisis result shows each side on a
  Mistake / Delayed / Sound scale. A new technology offers its two choices as
  doors next to a dial of how disruptive it is.
- **Plain words, no sums.** Card descriptions and area effects no longer
  quote multipliers or percentages; Settings › Show the numbers still adds
  the arithmetic to the move preview.
- **Fixed:** after a crisis was scored, the side panel and Week in review
  still called it "this week" until the next week began.
- Two-player codes from 0.22.0 still work.
